match.reason: The bank point teaches curve sketching using calculus (intercepts, stationary points, edge behaviour), which is a different idea from slope fields that show gradient directions and sketch solution curves without solving a differential equation.

draft.title: Slope fields
card: A slope field is a grid of short line segments. For dy/dx = f(x, y), the segment at each point (x, y) has gradient f(x, y).
To draw one, put the x and y values of a grid point into f(x, y). Example: for dy/dx = x − y, at (3, 1) the gradient is 3 − 1 = 2.
Where f(x, y) = 0, the segment is flat. Where f(x, y) is positive the segment rises to the right, and where it is negative it falls.
A solution curve is drawn by starting at a given point and following the segments, so that the curve touches each segment it meets and has the same direction there. No solving is needed.
draft.remember: Each segment shows the gradient f(x, y) at its point. A solution curve follows the segments.

a.q: A slope field is drawn for dy/dx = x − y. What is the gradient of the segment at the point (4, 1)?
a.why: Substitute x = 4 and y = 1: 4 − 1 = 3. The value 5 comes from adding the values instead of subtracting, and −3 comes from reversing the order to y − x.
a.clue: Put both coordinates into the right side of the equation.

b.q: For dy/dx = xy, which statement about the slope field is correct?
opts: Segments are flat along both axes
Segments are flat only along the x-axis
Segments are flat only along the y-axis
Segments are flat only at the origin
b.why: The gradient is xy, which is 0 when x = 0 or y = 0. So segments are flat along both axes. Flat only at the origin is tempting, but every point on either axis gives xy = 0.

b.best: Segments are flat along both axes

final.title: Slope fields
card: A slope field is a grid of short line segments. For \(\frac{dy}{dx} = f(x, y)\), the segment at each point \((x, y)\) has gradient \(f(x, y)\).
To draw one, put the \(x\) and \(y\) values of a grid point into \(f(x, y)\). Example: for \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x - y\), at \((3, 1)\) the gradient is \(3 - 1 = 2\).
Where \(f(x, y) = 0\), the segment is flat. Where \(f(x, y)\) is positive the segment rises to the right, and where it is negative it falls.
A solution curve is drawn by starting at a given point and following the segments, so that the curve touches each segment it meets and has the same direction there. No solving is needed.
final.remember: Each segment shows the gradient \(f(x, y)\) at its point. A solution curve follows the segments.

a.q: A slope field is drawn for \(\frac{dy}{dx} = x - y\). What is the gradient of the segment at the point \((4, 1)\)?
a.why: Substitute \(x = 4\) and \(y = 1\): \(4 - 1 = 3\). The value 5 comes from adding the values instead of subtracting, and \(-3\) comes from reversing the order to \(y - x\).
a.clue: Put both coordinates into the right side of the equation.

b.q: For \(\frac{dy}{dx} = xy\), which statement about the slope field is correct?
opts: Segments are flat along both axes
Segments are flat only along the x-axis
Segments are flat only along the y-axis
Segments are flat only at the origin
b.why: The gradient is \(xy\), which is 0 when \(x = 0\) or \(y = 0\). So segments are flat along both axes. Flat only at the origin is tempting, but every point on either axis gives \(xy = 0\).
